wi.est_size: About 170 contests (72 sheriffs, 71-72 clerks of circuit court, about 28 coroners); perhaps 200-250 candidates.
wi.build_plan: There is no statewide list, so a Wisconsin loader would work county by county from a hand-kept table of the 72 county clerks' election pages (starting from the Commission's own list of county election websites), holding for each the address of one November 2026 sample ballot or, failing that, the clerk's candidate list. It would fetch what scripts can reach through states/net.py, read each PDF in memory with ballot/pdftext.py, and keep only the ballot's County section (Sheriff, Clerk of Circuit Court, Coroner): name, party and ballot order, splitting the ballot's three printed columns by position. Counties whose sites refuse scripts (Milwaukee, Brown and Dane's pages so far) wait for files John saves, and a county with nothing readable is listed as a gap, never guessed. Each county is checked against its own official August 11 primary canvass; cities, towns, schools, judges and county boards are left for April, when Wisconsin elects them.
wi.privacy_slip: Minor, nothing saved or stored: a web-search summary named one Dane County candidate's town of residence; a masked layout print of Waukesha's filing list let one street-type word ("Court") through, with no name, number or street name; and two public-office contacts appeared (a county clerk's office address line in an election notice, a clerk's office phone in a search summary). No candidate address, phone, e-mail or website was printed.

On election night its results system, https://electionresults.iowa.gov/IA/, should carry all 99 counties' local contests; November is not posted yet.

ia.est_size: Not counted; my estimate: about 750 county-level contests, up to 3,200 township contests (1,599 townships), dozens of judges.
ia.build_plan: Iowa has no statewide list of local candidates before the election: county and township candidates file with each of the 99 county auditors, and the Secretary of State's list stops at the Legislature. The practical statewide route is the Secretary's results system, one keyless file layout for all 99 counties, which already carried county offices in June 2026 and city and school races in 2025; a loader written against those files would pick up November's contests, names and parties when that election is posted (not yet; perhaps only on election night). To show candidates sooner, a loader would have to go county by county, reading office, name and party from sample-ballot PDFs (no contact details) or from each auditor's candidate list while never reading its e-mail, phone and address columns; the four largest counties each use a different layout. Judges on the retention ballot would come from the Judicial Branch's voter's guide once its 2026 edition is posted (names and court only; today the page still shows 2024), and place names from county FIPS codes and the Census list of Iowa's townships.
ia.privacy_slip: One slip, nothing readable: a Cloudflare-scrambled e-mail link from Johnson County's election page (a hex code, not decoded, no name beside it, possibly a candidate's) was printed once, because the code happened to contain "2026". No candidate address, phone, e-mail or website was printed; contact cells were only counted. Office contact details of agencies and party headquarters (Secretary of State, county election offices, the two state parties) appeared in the Candidate's Guide text and in search summaries. Nothing fetched was written to disk.

mo.build_plan: Start with what the kit already downloads: the Secretary of State's certification lists the circuit judges and the yes/no retention votes, which the state loader (ballot/state_local_mo.py) now counts and skips. Then add county offices one election authority at a time, largest first, reading each county's own sample ballot or notice of election PDF for contest, district, name and party only (use the Jackson County election board's notice, not the county clerk's certificate, which prints addresses). Key each race to the county's FIPS code, and show every county not yet read as "list not loaded" rather than as empty. Say on the page that Missouri's cities, schools and special districts vote in April, so they are not on this ballot.

Then go county by county, reading each election office's Notice of Election or sample ballot PDF, starting with Douglas (now at votedouglascounty-ne.gov; the old .com address only redirects to the home page), Lancaster and Sarpy; layouts differ (one to three columns), so each county needs its own reader and a check that every office heading was found. Printed, allowed fields only: 28 judges' names with court and district (that list has no contact columns) and seven candidate names caught by heading filters in the Douglas and Lancaster notices (neither has contact columns). Agency details only: the Secretary of State's own office address and fax number from the filing guide, and fragments of town website addresses from the Secretary's Cities and Villages directory.

tn.build_plan: No statewide list exists, so a loader would work county by county from each election commission's official November sample ballot (a PDF with a text layer; Hamilton posts a web page). It would need a hand-checked table of the 95 county offices' sample-ballot addresses, read each ballot column by column, and keep only the city contests: title, city, ward or position, the 'vote for' number and the names in printed order. A city that lies in two counties (Oak Ridge, Oliver Springs, Goodlettsville) must read the same on each county's ballot, and a county with no city race in November (Knox) is recorded as having none. The counties' 'qualified candidates' lists are left alone because they carry addresses, phones and e-mail.

co.on_nov_ballot: Partisan county offices in 62 counties: one commissioner seat (two on five-member boards), clerk and recorder, treasurer, assessor, sheriff, coroner, surveyor (C.R.S. 1-4-205, 1-4-206). Nonpartisan: RTD directors in seven districts, retention votes for district and county court judges, towns that moved their elections to November of even years (a few dozen), and Denver's council at-large vacancy.
co.not_on_nov_ballot: School boards (November of odd years; next November 2, 2027). Special district boards (May of odd years, C.R.S. 1-13.5-111). Most towns (April, even years) and cities (November, odd years). Denver's regular offices (2027). District attorneys (not on the 2026 list). No townships.
co.source: Colorado Secretary of State, 2026 General Election Official Candidate List: https://www.coloradosos.gov/pubs/elections/vote/generalCandidates.html (Excel copy linked there). County and town contests appear statewide only on its results site, https://results.enr.clarityelections.com/CO/elections.json, where "2026 General" is not listed yet (checked 2026-09-30).
co.format: HTML table plus an XLSX copy; the results site is JSON, one file per county.
co.offices_covered: Local levels only partly: RTD Board of Directors (districts B, C, J, K, L, N, O) and retention of district, county, Denver juvenile and probate court judges. County officers and town offices are not in it.
co.columns: Candidate name, Office, District, Party, Write in?. A withdrawal shows as a struck-through name; ballot order comes from separate lot-drawing pages (parties; RTD petition candidates). Contact columns: no.
co.fetch_detail: 72,709 bytes, first bytes b'<!DOCTYP'; 404 rows, 5 columns. Results host's election list also answered (3,264 bytes); a county page of the June primary read fine.
co.county_route: 64 counties; each clerk posts its own page. El Paso: sample ballot PDF that is a picture (no text). Denver: HTML tables for state, judge and RTD races, council vacancy on a separate page, sample ballot PDFs without text. Arapahoe: HTML table of county candidates (has a Website column). Jefferson: HTML page, one heading per contest, names with party, website links. All four answered scripts. The state's "my ballot" site is a voter's own lookup: not usable.

co.est_size: Roughly 440 county contests, 117 judge retentions, 7 RTD seats (10 candidates); town contests maybe 30-60, unverified.
co.build_plan: Easy part now: the kit already reads the Secretary of State's list, and a loader can keep its 127 local rows (10 RTD candidates and 117 judges up for retention), filed by county name, judicial district or RTD letter. County and town candidates have no statewide list before the election: the Secretary's results site will add a "2026 General" entry (watch elections.json; when it opens was not verified) with one JSON file per county giving contest, names and party codes, and one loader could then read all 64 counties; the November 2022 pages show it carries county offices, town offices, RTD and judges. Until then it is county by county, each in its own format: Arapahoe, Jefferson and Denver post pages a script can read (the website links must be left unread), while El Paso's and Denver's sample ballots are pictures. The Secretary's municipal results CSV (Results/municipalResults.html, no contact columns) shows which towns already voted in April, so they are not expected in November.

A helper that lists a page's links printed six candidate website addresses beside the candidates' names: five state or federal candidates on Jefferson County's page and one county candidate on Arapahoe County's page. Nothing was saved to disk, and the helper was then changed to print government links only. A site configuration file also printed the Secretary of State's own office address, phone and e-mail (an office, not a person). No addresses, phones or e-mail of any candidate were printed.

ky.on_nov_ballot: County offices, all partisan: judge/executive, clerk, attorney, sheriff, jailer, coroner, PVA, surveyor, magistrates or commissioners, constables. Cities: mayors whose terms are up and every council or commission, mostly nonpartisan. School boards (staggered seats) and soil and water supervisors (only if contested), nonpartisan. District judges, nonpartisan; a few unexpired circuit judge, circuit clerk and Commonwealth's attorney terms.
ky.not_on_nov_ballot: Governor and statewide officers (2027). Full terms of circuit judges, circuit clerks, Commonwealth's attorneys (2030). Other mayors, school board seats, even Louisville council districts (2028). Fire district trustees vote in June (KRS 75.031). No townships or spring elections.
ky.source: Kentucky Secretary of State, "Candidate Filings with the County Clerk", https://web.sos.ky.gov/CandidateFilings/countyfilings.aspx (its buttons "List All Candidates" and "Excel spreadsheet of All Candidates"). Local judges are on the sister page, https://web.sos.ky.gov/CandidateFilings/Default.aspx?id=17 (also id=13, 16, 20).

ky.offices_covered: All 120 counties: every county office, magistrates, commissioners, constables, mayors, city councils and commissions, school boards, soil and water supervisors, circuit court clerks. District and circuit judges and Commonwealth's attorneys are on the sister page.
ky.columns: County, name (last, first, middle, suffix), party, office, office description (free text naming the city or school district, often blank), district number, date filed, unexpired, withdrawn, disqualified, deceased. No ballot order. Contact columns also present: yes.

ky.county_route: Not needed for the names: the state list covers all 120 counties. As a check on what is printed, the Secretary of State posts 116 counties' November sample ballots as PDFs at web.sos.ky.gov/electionballots/ (none for Jefferson, Breathitt, Floyd, Knott). Scripts fetch them, but they are scans with machine-read text and errors. Jefferson's clerk posts its own 49-page list (text PDF, script fetch works, e-mail addresses in it). Fayette, Kenton, Boone and Warren are on the state page.

ky.est_size: About 6,500 candidates on the county list (135 write-ins) plus 138 judicial; roughly 3,300 contests.
ky.build_plan: Post the county filings page's own Excel button once with the honest User-Agent (form field ctl00$MainContent$bExcel plus the page's hidden fields, as the North Dakota loader posts its form), read the old-format .xls in memory with a small reader (the kit has none yet; a 70-line one worked in this test), and keep only allowlisted columns: county, name parts, party, office, office description, district and the four status flags, never the PO or e-mail columns. County offices, magistrates, commissioners and constables key cleanly by county and district number; cities and school boards need the free-text description matched to official place and school district names, and a row that names no place (about one in eight council rows) goes to a gap list, never a guess. Where one party is listed more than once for a seat (Casey, Metcalfe, Carlisle and a few other counties still show May primary losers), and for soil and water races, which are not printed when uncontested (KRS 262.240), check the county's sample ballot on the Secretary of State's Election Ballots page before loading. District judges and the few unexpired circuit seats come from the Secretary of State's own filings pages with the reader the Kentucky loaders already use (the Family Court page, id=20, did not pass that reader's heading check: not verified why); the state results site (vrsws.sos.ky.gov/liveresults) answered a script with 403, so results after November 3 may need John's browser.

Two web-search summaries showed county election offices' own public phone, street address and office e-mail (offices, not candidates), and a few candidates' filing dates. Nothing fetched was saved to disk by me; the harness kept one oversized printout of the State Board's election calendar (dates and statute citations only) in its own tool-results folder.

Nonpartisan: a few cities (Bartlesville, Clinton, El Reno, Lawton, Yukon, a Tulsa runoff), fire protection district boards (19 O.S. 901.5), district and associate district judges. No school boards or townships.

ok.format: One HTML page of nested tables: county, section, office, candidate line.

Write one small reader per layout (list-style certifications like Salt Lake, Utah County and Millard; ballot-style PDFs like Davis and Weber), keeping only contest, party and name in the printed order, starting with the four largest counties; never open the per-candidate PDFs that a county candidate page links to (Weber's does), since filed declarations carry home addresses. Add the 30 justice-court retention questions from the Lieutenant Governor's certification that ballot/state_local_ut.py already reads and today only counts. ks.build_plan: Kansas has no statewide list of county or township candidates, so the loader would be a set of county readers fed by a hand-kept table of the 105 county election offices' candidate pages and Notices of General Election. Start with the formats that repeat: the CSV Sedgwick posts (the same columns as the Secretary of State's list, so the column-by-name reading in C:\Users\16516\plain-congress\ballot\lists\ks.py fits), the candidatefiling.us pages Shawnee and Douglas use, Johnson's candidate view, then text PDF notices for the rest. Every one of these lists also carries addresses, phones or e-mail, so each reader must work in memory, take only office, district or township, name and party by heading, and keep a small extract, never the file. Races would be keyed by county FIPS plus the township's Census code or the commissioner district number, with no ballot order (none is published); a county whose site refuses scripts (Leavenworth's file host failed its secure handshake once) falls to John's browser.

ca.build_plan: There is no statewide file, so California would be a set of county readers under one frame: fetch each registrar's candidate list PDF with net.py and read it with ballot/pdftext.py by column edge, turning into text only the contest, name, party and on-ballot cells (Los Angeles and San Bernardino print address, phone, e-mail and website beside them, so those bands must never be joined). tx.not_on_nov_ballot: Sheriffs, tax assessors, most constables and county attorneys, commissioners for precincts 1 and 3 (presidential years). Many cities, schools and special districts vote on the May uniform date (May 2, 2026). No townships. Unopposed local elections can be cancelled.

pa.build_plan: The page should first say, citing the Constitution (Article VII section 3), Election Code section 602 and the Department of State's "Types of Elections" page, that Pennsylvania elects its county, municipal, school and local court offices in odd-numbered years, so none is regularly on this ballot. The few exceptions (a council seat filled by special election, an elected study commission) appear only in each county's own postings, so a loader would read every county's list of offices on the ballot (each board prepares a notice of offices for military and overseas voters, and the counties checked post it) and keep whatever is not a state or federal office. For those few contests it would then read that county's candidate list, taking only office, place, name, party and order, never the address and city columns Allegheny's workbook carries. Until all 67 counties are read, the page should name the counties checked, and the lists should be re-read close to the election because Allegheny's says it is still being updated.
